record.paper_title: Electrostatic models for zeros of polynomials: old, new, and some open problems
record.original_question: For Freud-type orthogonal polynomials obtained by perturbing the Freud weight e^{-x^4} with an added fixed charge λ at the origin, do the zeros always form a stable equilibrium, meaning that they realize the global minimum of the total energy, or is there a critical value λ₀(n) such that the zeros minimize the energy only for 0 ≤ λ < λ₀(n) and cease to be stable for λ > λ₀(n)?

evidence.quote: But can we assure that they are in a stable equilibrium, that is, that E(X∗) = min E(X)? The complete answer is not clear yet. By computing the Hessian matrix H (2.9) it was proved that for small values of the correction charge λ this is really the case, but there are some evidences that make it possible to conjecture the existence of a critical value λ0 such that for 0 ≤ λ < λ0(n) the zeros of the orthogonal polynomials attain the minimum of the total energy, but for λ > λ0(n) the equilibrium is no longer stable.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix an integer n ≥ 1 and a real parameter λ ≥ 0. Consider the perturbed Freud weight on the real line
   w_λ(x) = |x|^{2λ} e^{-x^4},
and let p_n(x;λ) be the monic orthogonal polynomial of degree n with respect to w_λ. Let X* = (x_1, …, x_n) denote the (real) zeros of p_n(·;λ). These zeros are known to be critical points of the total electrostatic energy
   E(X) = -∑_{i<j} log|x_i - x_j| + (1/2)∑_i Q(x_i),
where the external field is Q(x) = x^4 - 2λ log|x| (so a fixed charge λ is placed at the origin).

Question: For every n, do the zeros X* always realize the global minimum of E, i.e. E(X*) = min_X E(X) for all λ ≥ 0? Or does there exist a critical value λ_0(n) > 0 such that X* is a global minimizer of E precisely for 0 ≤ λ < λ_0(n), and ceases to be a stable equilibrium (a global minimizer) for λ > λ_0(n)? Determine which alternative holds, and in the latter case characterize λ_0(n).
artifact.status_search_result: A web search on perturbed Freud weights e^{-x^4} with a charge at the origin and stability of zero configurations did not return a definitive resolution of the conjectured existence of a critical λ_0(n). Recent work on singularly perturbed Freud weights focuses on recurrence coefficients, Painlevé hierarchies, and asymptotic zero distributions, but does not appear to confirm or refute the stability/critical-value question. Status therefore remains unclear from available sources.

status_evidence.title: Orthogonal Polynomials with Singularly Perturbed Freud Weights
status_evidence.snippet: Studies singularly perturbed Freud-type weights and properties of associated orthogonal polynomials, without addressing global-minimum stability of zero configurations.
status_evidence.claim: Recent literature on perturbed Freud weights does not directly settle the stability/critical-charge question.

status_evidence.title: Generalised higher-order Freud weights (arXiv:2211.13645)
status_evidence.snippet: Treats hierarchies of higher-order Freud weights, recurrence coefficients and limiting zero distributions; does not establish a critical λ_0(n) for global energy minimality.
status_evidence.claim: No resolution of the electrostatic stability question is given.
